<reason>B won the motion as written by forcing a fork: after A conceded that opted-in, disable-able jealousy and ordinary subscription cutoffs after bonding are legitimate, leftover harms (ignored controls, payment-conditioned panic, abusive collection) fit CON’s deception/coercion standard without a special duty of care. A’s product story was more vivid, but never showed why those leftovers require treating companions as a distinct legal category rather than ordinary entertainment plus consumer rules.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B’s second rebuttal used A’s A1/A2 concessions to collapse “paywalled intimacy” and retention-optimized tropes into ordinary authorization-and-collection questions, leaving “feels like cruelty” as an effect of fiction A had already allowed.</best_rebuttal>
